nodes.name: Fe NPs synthesis
nodes.procedure: All reactions were carried out under an inert nitrogen atmosphere. Firstly, 0.3 g of FeSO4·7H2O and 0.25 g of PVP were dissolved in 100 ml of deionized water and stirred for 30 minutes (solution A). Secondly, 0.1 g NaBH4 and 0.125 g PVP were dissolved in 50 ml of deionized water (solution B). Then solution B was added to solution A drop by drop and stirred for 90 minutes to obtain the Fe NPs. The product was centrifuged at 5000 rpm for 5 min to discard the supernatant and the solid was dispersed in 50 ml 0.25% PVP.

nodes.name: Fe@Pt core-shell formation
nodes.procedure: Then, a mixture of 0.112 g K2PtCl4 and 0.125 g PVP in 50 ml deionized water was added [to the Fe NPs dispersion] and stirred for 3 h. The reaction product was centrifuged and washed with deionized water, 0.1 M H2SO4 solution and deionized water three times. The final product was dried under vacuum at 60°C for 24 h. The dried sample was ground evenly with a mortar and kept sealed. All reactions were carried out under an inert nitrogen atmosphere.

nodes.name: Fe@Pt/C catalyst preparation
nodes.procedure: The obtained core–shell Fe@Pt catalyst was dispersed in conductive carbon black by a simple physical mixing method, and the Fe@Pt/C catalyst for membrane electrode preparation was obtained.
nodes.source_text: the obtained core–shell Fe@Pt catalyst was dispersed in conductive carbon black by a simple physical mixing method

nodes.name: Fe@Pt/C/PTFE membrane electrode fabrication
nodes.procedure: The electrode slurry was composed of the catalytic material (Fe@Pt/C), linking agent (HEC), surfactant (Triton X-100), PTFE emulsion, leveling agent (BYK-333), defoaming agent (BYK-094), deionized water and ethanol. First, a transparent and moderate viscosity HEC solution was obtained by dissolving a certain amount of HEC in an equal volume of ethanol and water (the mass ratio of HEC to deionized water is 0.04). Suck 0.6 ml HEC solution, 0.2 ml 10 wt% Triton X-100 solution, 0.05 ml 10 wt% PTFE lotion, 0.1 ml 10 wt% BYK-333 solution, 0.1 ml 10 wt% BYK-094 solution in turn, and mix the above solutions evenly with 0.1 g Fe@Pt/C catalyst. Subsequently, the membrane electrode was printed on the PTFE film using the screen printing process. The PTFE film is sequentially pretreated in dilute sulfuric acid, deionized water and ethanol at 60°C for one hour. The electrode slurry is evenly printed on the PTFE film with a scraper. The obtained membranes were dried at 60°C for 6 hours for the first time, and the impurities were removed by washing with water. The final membrane electrodes were obtained by vacuum drying at 180°C for 3 hours.

nodes.description: H2S detection performance at optimal conditions (0.3 V)
nodes.source_text: Through the detection of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) with different concentrations, it is found that the sensor strictly shows linear correlation in the range of 1–20 ppm, R² = 0.99974. Notably, the sensor exhibits high sensitivity (658.45 nA ppm⁻¹) and a low detection limit of 0.33 ppm. Moreover, the consistency and stability of the sensor are satisfactory.

nodes.description: Optimization of working potential for H2S detection
nodes.source_text: when the content of PTFE emulsion was 0.05 ml, the sensitivity of the H2S gas sensor reached the maximum of 664.2 nA ppm⁻¹.

A platinum black film was used to construct the sensor and cyclic voltammetry (CV) was used to study the redox status of 50 ppm H2S. The oxidation current begins to appear when the working electrode potential is about 0 V. And the oxidation current reaches the peak at about 0.4 V.

interfering_gases.value: NO2, Cl2, NH3, C2H4, H2, CO, NO, SO2

selectivity.value: low cross-sensitivity to NO2 and SO2

nodes.source_text: To evaluate the selectivity of the prepared gas sensor to H2S, the common interfering gases (NO2, Cl2, NH3, C2H4, H2, CO, NO, and SO2) with different concentrations were also tested... The results show that even NO2 and SO2, which are the most easily disturbed gases in the measurement process, have relatively low cross-sensitivity.
the influence of temperature on zero point and sensitivity is also explored... In the range of -30 to 30 degrees, the change of zero point and sensitivity is within 20%, which is relatively stable.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows slightly agglomerated spherical structure composed of relatively uniform-sized nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1A and B, the SEM image of the Fe@Pt catalyst appears as a slightly agglomerated spherical structure composed of relatively uniform-sized nanoparticles stacked together.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows uniformly distributed spherical morphology with size of about 50 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image shows a uniformly distributed spherical morphology with a size of about 50 nm (Fig. 1C).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice stripes of 0.224 nm (Pt, 111) and 0.202 nm (Fe, 110) with no obvious discontinuity and shell thickness of about 10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And the HRTEM partially enlarged view of Fig. 1D shows the lattice stripe of 0.224 nm (Pt, 111) and 0.202 nm (Fe, 110), which determines the successful preparation of the Fe@Pt nanocomposite.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM with insets showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM mapping shows Fe and Pt elements almost uniformly distributed on spherical nanostructures with more element distribution on the outer shell compared to the interior.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM mapping images are shown in Fig. 1E–H; the Fe element and Pt element are almost uniformly distributed on spherical nanostructures.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of Pt (111), (200), (220), (311) crystal planes but no characteristic peaks of Fe element.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of the Fe@Pt core–shell materials are shown in Fig. 2A, where the (111) (200) (220) (311) crystal plane is the characteristic peak of the Pt element...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows strong Pt 4d, 4f and Fe 2p orbitals. Before etching: Pt 4f shows elemental Pt (71.4 eV, 74.4 eV) > Pt2+ (72.9 eV, 75.9 eV); Fe 2p shows Fe2+ (711.1 eV, 734.3 eV) > elemental Fe (707.1 eV, 720.1 eV). After 10 nm etching, elemental Pt ratio increases significantly and elemental Fe content increases substantially.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS images of the 4f orbitals of Pt and the 2p orbitals of Fe before etching are shown in Fig. 2C and D, respectively... After etching, the atomic ratio of elemental Pt to Pt2+ increases significantly... the content of elemental Fe increased significantly after etching.
